newsitem.title: UK: UK to allow divorcees to divide up pensions.
newsitem.headline: UK to allow divorcees to divide up pensions.

text.p: Britain's new Labour government said on Thursday it will allow divorced couples to share pensions, although the plan is unlikely to become law until the year 2000.

"I will introduce pension-sharing for divorcing couples. This is an important step towards meeting the government's objectives of improving the income of women in retirement," Social Security Secretary Harriet Harman said in a written parliamentary reply.
"It is the combination of the basic state pension and a decent second pension which prevents people from retiring into poverty. But women are less likely than men to have a good second pension."
The move will end the existing system whereby a divorcee can only claim a share of an ex-partner's pension when that pension is taken.

Harman said she planned to introduce a system which will enable divorcees to make a clean financial break with former spouses by allowing them to take part of a former spouse's pension fund upon divorce.

"My proposals will lead to fairer treatment of pensions in financial settlements between divorcing couples and will provide a better and more secure income in retirement for those receiving a share of pension rights," she said.
